To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we describe a unique case report of HJMD and DNAH5- related PCD in a young Indian girl with novel variants in CDH3 and DNHAS.
we report a unique case of vision impairment due to a CDH3 mutation with juvenile macular degeneration and primary ciliary dysfunction due to a DNAH5 mutation.
we report the first case of CDH13-related hypotrichoses with juvenile macular degeneration (HJMD).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mutations in the CDH 3 and DNAH 5 genes that are associated with HJMD and CDH, respectively.
the genetic and clinical features of a patient with a rare disease that is associated with a unique combination of HJMD and ciliary dyskinesis
the genetic analysis of two novel variants, CDH3 c.[1660A ≥ C; p.Thr554Pro] and DNAH5 [c.6688- 1G>T] in a patient with HJMD and DNAH5 -related PCD with progressive vision loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this patient had a novel combination of HJMD and DNAH5 PCD.
this patient has HJMD and CDH3 mutation and also has PCD and DNAH5 mutation, and that the CDH3 gene mutation is a new finding in HJMD.
this case represents a unique combination of HJMD and ciliary dysfunction with progressive vision loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of CDH3 and PCD mutations in the same patient is a unique finding.
this case is unique in its presentation with both HJMD, PCD, and hypotrichosis.
this case report is the first to document a patient with CDH3-related HJMD and DNAH5-PCD with progressive vision loss and is the first to report a CDH3 mutation in an Indian female.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HJMD and DNAH5 mutations can coexist in the same patient and can be associated with progressive vision loss.
HJMD is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder that can present with vision loss, hypotrichiosis, and hearing loss, and that the disease is progressive.
HJMD can be an important cause of visual impairment in young children, and that the diagnosis of HJMD can have important implications for the management of patients with PCD.
